name: Oxygen
occurrence: Makes up 21% of the atmosphere and is the most abundant element in Earth's crust by mass, mostly bound in silicates and water.
biologicalRelevance: The final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration — without it, your mitochondria can't generate ATP efficiently, which is why you can survive minutes without it but weeks without food.
notableCharacteristics: Second most electronegative element after fluorine, and its diatomic form is unusual among stable molecules for having two unpaired electrons (making liquid O₂ visibly attracted to magnets).
whyHere: Six valence electrons leave it two short of a stable octet, so it grabs electrons aggressively in bonding — explaining both its high electronegativity and its central role as the electron acceptor in combustion and respiration.
didYouKnow: Liquid oxygen is pale blue and is one of the very few common liquids that's measurably paramagnetic — it gets pulled toward a strong magnet.
genZNote: Keeps you alive and also keeps things on fire. Multitasking at a molecular level, unpaired electrons and all.
